subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should `openclaw status` report a live memory plugin as healthy from gateway runtime-manager status even when embedding readiness is skipped, failed, or owned by the plugin?
rationale: The current code avoids the old false `unavailable` wording but still has no runtime-health field, while the available fix paths trade off gateway contract shape, local status side effects, and plugin-owned health semantics.

options.title: Replace with runtime-health contract
options.body: Close or replace the conflicting fork PR and land a core status/doctor contract that separates runtime health from embedding readiness with tests for human and JSON status.

options.title: Adopt the narrow provider fallback
options.body: Repair the open fork PR and prove it fixes the reported plugins, accepting that it may not solve the broader local status side-effect issue.

options.title: Accept current mitigation
options.body: Decide that `not checked` is the intended status behavior when runtime health is not explicitly probed, then close this issue with that product rationale.

recommendation.title: Replace with runtime-health contract
recommendation.body: Close or replace the conflicting fork PR and land a core status/doctor contract that separates runtime health from embedding readiness with tests for human and JSON status.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle authored the current status mitigation and is the strongest recent history signal for the affected status surface.
